title: Replicating Safety Index Analysis Across Time: 2022 vs. 2025 Frontier Lab Governance

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: tests whether governance improvements are real or cosmetic by applying current rubric retroactively. Clear policy implications either way.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: retroactive application of a rubric to archived documentation requires careful methodology and judgment about how to handle missing data and document format changes.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: collecting archived documentation from Web Archive, applying FLI rubric retroactively, and comparing to current scores. Feasible but requires methodological care.

novelty.reasoning: The FLI AI Safety Index was first launched in late 2024. The Summer 2025 edition showed temporal changes (e.g., OpenAI improved in transparency, DeepMind fell in relative ranking). However, no published work has retroactively applied the current FLI rubric to 2022-era company documentation using Web Archive snapshots. The FLI index itself notes that governance practices have evolved, but does not provide a historical baseline. The methodological challenge of applying a 2025 rubric to 2022 documents is acknowledged but not attempted. This idea fills a genuine gap: determining whether governance improvements are substantive or cosmetic by providing a pre-index baseline. The approach is novel though methodologically demanding.
